responsibility: Implements the Renesas RX target backend’s C-side hook logic that complements rx.md and rx.h. This file owns the RX-specific target hooks for argument passing and return values, prologue/epilogue and trampoline emission, register usage and hard-register mode rules, address legitimacy and address legalization (including small-data and PID-based addressing), section selection, builtin initialization/expansion, operand and address printing, option override processing, cost modeling, and assorted RTL peephole or helper routines used during code generation. In practice it consumes GCC trees, RTL, target option state, and RX machine-description helpers, and produces target decisions and emitted RTL/assembly behavior for the RX port.
same_name_distinction: Contains the executable C implementation of the RX port’s backend hooks and helper routines—e.g. address legitimacy/legalization, builtin expansion, operand printing, option override, and TARGET_* hook bindings that instantiate `targetm`. Unlike rx.h, it defines behavior rather than target macros; unlike rx.md, it does not encode instruction patterns/scheduling; and unlike rx.opt, it is not the option-definition table.
